shown.evidence: In-memory removal of only BINDING constants/helpers, optional diagnostic sinks/call sites, V2 report field, installer import/envelope sanitization and receipt field reproduces both complete accepted prior source byte hashes. Earlier dirty-worktree changes are not attributed to this patch.

shown.claim: Refusal parity and full inventory retained
shown.evidence: After removing diagnostic calls/labels, _bindings and _configured_bindings comparisons match prior function bytes exactly. Every existing false return remains false. Full metadata traversal, selected network shape/created-only eligibility, projection, ports/DNS/mount/alias checks and unselected ownership scans remain. Legacy malformed raw-helper exceptions are not converted into successes; configured wrapper still fails closed.

The patch introduces only in-memory labels, category checks, sanitization and existing receipt serialization. It adds no transport/native command, read/capture, socket, lifecycle request, source inspection or retry. Existing network-inspect sequence is retained.

Exact schema/field set, fixed predicate/category/role enums, approved seven selected names only, and null target for unselected/none. Type checks precede label set membership, including malformed/unhashable labels. Unknown fields/labels and invalid role/target combinations sanitize to null. No arbitrary network/container name, metadata, exception text/class name, token or environment value is copied.

Legacy compatibility remains a boolean map; prior two-field and new three-field V2 envelopes are accepted at the installer boundary. The optional field is sanitized independently before receipt. Existing compatibility booleans alone determine acceptance; dropping an invalid diagnostic cannot convert a false gate to true.

Valid sanitized reasons appear in runtime_compatibility_checks before refusal/owned cleanup. False compatibility reaches no replacement-start or cited-query call. Per-call V2 diagnostic dictionaries avoid stale reasons; successful reports emit null.

remaining_limits.detail: This patch does not reconstruct the lost activated v6c metadata or identify the historical recipient subcause. No new observed reason or runtime success is claimed.

First failure follows current traversal order and is not a unique root cause. Later checks may be unevaluated. Combined predicates retain combined labels; malformed legacy-helper data may yield the broader recipient_policy/exception category. Timeout/refused/invalid_input/operation_error are bounded categories, not detailed traces.

Successful calls emit null in the V2 report, and legacy boolean maps remain unchanged. Direct helper callers supplying their own diagnostic sink own that sink; no broader persistent diagnostic store or new observation framework is introduced.

Current changed consumer hashes intentionally invalidate frozen wrapper/packet current-source bindings. No accepted policy, scope, packet, preparation or execution wrapper is rebound by this review; any future applicability refresh needs its separate exact binding review.

Final alias/attachment behavior, live SDK/import/startup, recipient health, clock/pidfd/worker ownership, acknowledgement/recovery, cited retrieval, volume integrity and economics remain outside offline proof. Existing consumed attempts and removed stage IDs must not be retried/reset or adopted.
